findings.issue: handsPlayed and nextBotId are accepted up to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. restoreSession then sets handNumber = handsPlayed + 1, and nextHand increments nextBotId, so either can step past the safe range.
findings.evidence: DevTools-edited sessions record {handsPlayed: 9007199254740991} -> parseSessionRecord passes (whole >= 0) -> restoreSession handNumber = 2^53 -> the next combined write stores a hand/session that later fails parseHandRecord/parseSessionRecord. This fails closed (RangeError on read, no crash, no information exposure) and the restore path has no UI consumer yet (getSession only), so nothing is exploitable.
findings.fix: Optional: cap handsPlayed and nextBotId below MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (e.g. max = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - 1), or leave it as is and note it as fail-closed in docs/storage/sessions.md.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. I traced the restore trust boundary (IndexedDB -> getSession -> parseSessionRecord -> restoreSession) field by field. (1) Types are checked before use: Number.isSafeInteger/isWhole without coercion; typeof string before the sessionId regex and ISO parsing; Array.isArray plus an index-loop density check for config.seats and record.seats; isRecord/object rejects arrays and null; stake fields are typeof number before stakesFor; isReplayCode now rejects non-strings; echoValue never calls a hostile toString. Huge or sparse arrays fail on the length-vs-players check before any loop. (2) Prototype keys: hand/actions use Object.hasOwn. Structured-clone data has no getters or custom prototypes, and an own '__proto__' key is harmless. (3) Bounds: seats 1..10 strictly ascending, players in TABLE_SIZES and equal to seats.length, names 1-40 characters, botIds unique and in 1..nextBotId-1, level tied to the game type, and stakes and stacks go through the engine's assertChips (positive safe integers, total <= MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so every pot and contribution is bounded). parseHandRecord adds bounds (400 actions, 10 seat entries) and seat-membership, one-pair-per-seat and no-repeated-card checks. (4) REQ-025: assertSessionConfig requires exactly one user seat with seat === userSeat, and parseSessionRecord requires record.seats[i].seat and .kind to equal config.seats[i], so the restored TableState cannot make a bot seat the user's view. The session record stores no hole cards and no replay code (sessionRecord omits replayCode, and restoreSession sets replayCode: null). (5) No HandState or action injection: hand/actions are rejected, restoreSession always returns hand: null and userDecisions: [], and it never calls applyAction or createHand. (6) No native TypeError on hostile shapes: every property access is guarded by the object/array checks, and config.seats[i] is only indexed after the density and length checks. nextReplacementName at the maximum nextBotName throws a RangeError and its loop is bounded by the 10 seated names. Write path: the session id is CSPRNG (unchanged), the combined write is one strict transaction, and the logged errors contain no secrets. No new dependencies. Restore is not yet reachable from the UI (only HandStore.getSession), so all of this is defence ahead of the Resume story. One NIT: the counters are unbounded up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, which fails closed.
